title: Network statistics of the whole-brain connectome of Drosophila
dataset: FAFB v630 (127,978 neurons; 2,613,129 connections at >=5-synapse threshold)
question: Whole-brain network organization
method: Rich-club vs CFG/NND/NPC nulls; 2- and 3-node motif enumeration with NT composition; neuropil subnetworks; degree-ordered neuron-removal survival curves (SCC persistence); spectral attractor/repeller walks
main_result: Rich-club ~30% of neurons; giant SCC 93.3% / WCC 98.8%; reciprocity 0.138; ach-GABA and ach-glut reciprocal pairs over-represented; neurons with high reciprocal degree (drec>100) mostly GABAergic; high-total-degree neurons mostly GABAergic; FFLs with 1 inhibitory edge = feedforward inhibition, 2 = disinhibition (descriptive)
uses_neurotransmitter_sign: Yes - motif/reciprocity composition by NT sign
uses_perturbation_or_node_removal: Yes - degree-ORDERED survival curves only (SCC splitting; NOT per-neuron impact ranking; NOT NT-conditioned)
uses_null_model: Yes - CFG, ER, NND, NPC models
notes: CRITICAL: used v630, NOT v783. Did degree-ordered removal (Fig 1f,g + ED Fig 2a-d) but no per-neuron control-impact ranking and no NT-conditioned perturbation. Their ED Fig 3d finding (high-degree neurons mostly GABAergic) means our baseline GABA-strength signal is a REPLICATION of theirs, not a novel finding.
